newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Perstorp says to sell Perstorp Analytical.
newsitem.headline: Perstorp says to sell Perstorp Analytical.

text.p: Swedish chemical group Perstorp said on Thursday it would sell Perstorp Analytical for a capital gain of about 150 million crowns.
The sale is part of the company's aim to streamline operations and followed a December 1996 divestment of the business area Perstorp Components, it said in its six-month results report.
Perstorp posted a 33 percent drop in six-month pre-tax profit to 208 million crowns and lowered its full-year forecast by 100 million crowns because of structural measures.

"The annual report's forecast for a full-year result around the same level as in the previous year (716 million crowns) has been reduced with net costs for the mentioned structural changes of about 100 million crowns," it said.
Perstorp also said it aimed to lower its costs.

"To strengthen the group's competitiveness an extensive productivity enhancing programme will start with the aim of lowering costs by at least 500 million crowns within a three-year period," the company said.
The programme included concentrating European operations in the divisions Perstorp Surfaces and Plastic Systems to fewer and larger units, while divesting remaining Components operations in Germany.
The cost cutting programme was part of a larger plan, which will run to the year 2000, to further increase long-term growth and profitability, it said.
The plan also included focusing on core operations and a new organisation with larger business areas from February 1 this year.
"The world leading positions in the chemical area will be developed strongly through continued geographical expansion and new product applications," the company said.
"The leading global position within laminate floors will be further strengthened through increased market penetration and expansion on new markets."
The company would also focus on Construction Chemicals and Life Science and the unit Perstorp Plastic Systems intended to take part of the likely restructuring on the European market, it said.

Looking at the market, it said there was still uncertainty regarding economic trends. But when excluding the sold unit Perstorp Components, volumes were strong despite weak economic trends, mainly in Europe, Perstorp said.
For the first six months of its financial year, Perstorp posted a turnover of 5.67 billion crowns, down from 6.37 billion crowns in the corresponding year earlier period.
Profit per share fell to 1.72 crowns from 2.81 crowns.
